questions.q: What does "what-if analysis" mean in Tableau, as described in this lesson?
options: Testing how results would change under a different input, using a parameter, without altering the underlying data
Permanently editing the connected data source to test new numbers
A dedicated Tableau menu item labeled exactly "What-If Analysis"
A feature exclusive to Tableau Server, unavailable in Desktop
questions.explain: What-if analysis is built from existing tools — parameters plus calculated fields (and often a reference line) — not a single dedicated menu; the data itself is never modified.

questions.q: How do you make a reference line's position come from a parameter instead of a fixed value?
options: Parameters can only control color, never reference line position
Reference lines can never be based on a parameter
In the Edit Reference Line dialog, choose the parameter from the Value dropdown instead of a fixed number or aggregation
You must delete the reference line and recreate the whole chart
questions.explain: The Value dropdown in the Edit Reference Line, Band, or Box dialog lists parameters right alongside aggregations like CNT(Orders) — selecting one makes the line move as the parameter's value changes.

questions.q: In the worked example, what does `(SUM([Profit]) / SUM([Sales])) - [Target Profit Margin]` measure?
options: The total number of orders in the data source
The gap between the actual profit margin and an adjustable target margin parameter
A fixed historical average that never changes
The count of distinct customers
questions.explain: This calculation compares the real, computed profit margin against whatever value the Target Profit Margin parameter currently holds — the core of a what-if comparison.

questions.q: What happens to the underlying data source when you run a what-if scenario in Tableau?
options: The what-if scenario permanently overwrites the connected database
Nothing — the data source is never modified; only the parameter's value and the calculations built on it change
The data source must be manually edited to reflect the new scenario
Tableau creates a duplicate copy of the entire data source automatically
questions.explain: What-if analysis works entirely at the parameter and calculation layer — the underlying data source is completely untouched, which is exactly what makes it safe to explore interactively.

questions.q: Why pair a movable target parameter with a reference line, rather than just a calculated field alone?
options: Reference lines are required before any calculated field can be created
A calculated field cannot use a parameter unless a reference line also references it
It makes the target visible directly on the chart, so viewers can see actual results against a live, adjustable target at a glance
It has no practical benefit over a calculated field alone
questions.explain: The calculated field does the comparison math; the parameter-driven reference line makes that same movable target visually obvious on the chart itself as someone adjusts it.
